findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional — The guide says to skip extra jobs when one Vitest run has fewer files than groups; `src/forge/templates/skill.md:62-64` gives the same instruction.
Case: normal use - A four-group job runs an API suite with three files followed by a web suite with twelve. If group 4 skips or finishes the job after counting the API files, it never runs its web shard. The required check can pass with web tests omitted. The guide needs to skip only that API invocation and continue with the job's remaining test runs.
findings.title: Functional: Skip only the current Vitest invocation

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done — The new rule conflicts with the pytest recipe immediately above it. `src/forge/templates/skill.md:1471-1473` recommends `fast_test = "forge test --pytest {base}"`, but `src/forge/fasttest.py:770-778` and `:824-846` retain non-pytest steps from the full `test` command when there is no Vitest or Jest step.
Case: normal use - A Python app whose full command is `pytest -q && npx playwright test` follows that recipe. Its pull request still runs Playwright, including on shared-input changes. The testing-page example at `src/forge/templates/conventions/testing.md:20-28` likewise sets only the full `test` command; when `fast_test` is absent, `src/forge/review.py:368-377` falls back to it. The guidance needs a working way to keep the browser step out of change runs while retaining it in the nightly command.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional — `src/forge/prcheck.py:409-413` disables the one-group shortcut unless the command has an explicit `{groups}` count and no fixed shard count.
Case: normal use - A repo uses Forge's automatic pytest-split integration without placeholders, as Forge itself does in `forge.toml:6-7`. Its generated workflow sets `one-group` to false at `.github/workflows/forge.yml:28`, so even a one-file change uses all six groups. The new guide says this saving is automatic, leaving a team diagnosing a runner queue unaware that its configuration prevents it.
findings.title: Functional: Qualify when small changes use one group

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - An existing app tries to follow the copy instructions before the later tasks land. Both current starter scripts still run browser tests for web or shared changes, and the TypeScript starter does not yet contain the `test-groups.mjs`, `timed-sequencer.mjs` or `--group` handling referenced here and in `src/forge/templates/conventions/testing.md:151-153`. Those changes belong to STARTER and TIMEGROUPS; the recipes become usable after those tasks ship.
